1.1: 1.1 And King David was old. JEROME, letter to Nepotian, volume 1. Does it not seem to you, if you follow the letter that kills, to be a fiction or the playthings of the Atellan farces? A cold old man is wrapped in garments and does not grow warm unless by the embrace of a young girl. Bathsheba was still alive, etc., down to and Rahab the harlot, in type of the Church, hung out the cord containing the mystery of blood, that Jericho perishing her house might be saved, whence of the saints it is said: These are they who came from the warmth of the house of Rechab, I Chronicles 2. And elsewhere: I came to send fire on the earth, Luke 12., etc., which being kindled in the hearts of the disciples compelled them to say: Was not our heart burning within us? ibid., 24. And when he was covered, etc. David suffered excessive cold, either because he was born of aged parents, or because he had shed much blood in battle, or rather from when he saw the angel striking the people he wasted away with violent fear, whence in the discomfort of cold he remained until death.
1.5: 1.5 But Adonijah. He signifies the Jewish people, who seems to be the elder son, because it first received the law, and despising the Gentile people, which by the grace of God was called later, thought that it alone reigned with the Lord. For Adonijah is interpreted lord ruler. But the people of the Church, with the true Solomon, that is our peaceful one, whose body it is, by divine ordinance is put into the kingdom, from which deservedly for unfaithfulness the elder son, that is the first people, is cast down.
2.5: 2.5 You also. David commanded Solomon about the just retribution of those who were a comfort to him, or who unjustly harmed him, whom he himself patiently bore. And the prophecy indicates what evil or good must happen in the future, which the true Solomon will fulfill. Meanwhile the patience of God often permits the good to be tried and the wicked to enjoy delights.
2.19: 2.19 Bathsheba therefore came to the king. RABANUS. Adonijah, with Bathsheba interceding, etc., down to nor the law, which the Jews suppose to be a helper for them before God.
2.36: 2.36 And you shall not go out, etc. The true Solomon commands us who dwell in Jerusalem never to go out. But if those once subject to us flee, let us not therefore go out to follow the tracks of the fugitives, lest while we wish to save the fleeing we ourselves perish, but rather let the dead bury the dead, and the eye, the hand, the foot that scandalizes, while there is time, let us pluck out and cut off from us.
3.4: 3.4 Solomon therefore went. In Gibeon was the greatest high place, where was the tabernacle which Moses made, and the bronze altar, on which Solomon offering a thousand victims merited a divine oracle.
3.14: 3.14 And if you walk in my ways, etc. Without keeping the commandments of God, no one can obtain long days, that is blessedness. GREGORY, Moralia book VIII, chapter 17. After the Lord illumines the darkness of our error with the light of his knowledge, etc., down to that we may be reformed to the substance of the promised incorruption. JEROME, letter 131, volume 1. Some suppose that this is to be understood of the Synagogue and the Church, etc., down to note also what the Church says against the Synagogue.
3.17: 3.17 I and this woman. Because after the resurrection of the Savior one was gathered from both peoples. He elegantly added: I gave birth in the room with her. For the Church from the Gentiles, which did not have the law and the prophets, gave birth in the house of the synagogue, and did not go out of the room, but went in. Hence: The king brought me into his chamber, Song of Songs 2. And: I will bring you into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her who conceived me, ibid., 3. RABANUS. If you consider Pilate washing his hands and saying: I am innocent of the blood of this just man, Matthew 27, and the centurion confessing: Truly this was the Son of God, Mark 15, and those who before the passion desire through Philip to see the Lord, you do not doubt that the Church first gave birth; and afterward the people of the Jews was born, for whom the Lord prayed: Father, forgive them, etc., and three thousand believed in one day and another five thousand. GREGORY. By nursing mothers the order of teachers, etc., down to they themselves receive their children whole and living, when in the supreme judgment they obtain from their life a perfect retribution.
3.19: 3.19 Dead. RABANUS. For while it follows the observance of the law and joins the grace of the Gospel to the law, it was covered with the error of darkness.
3.20: 3.20 She took my son. Living, namely: not to possess him but to kill him. For she did not do this out of love for the son, but out of hatred of her rival.
3.21: 3.21 And looking at him more carefully, etc. RABANUS. It is long to show how through Paul and other ecclesiastical men the Church understood that he was not her son, who was feared in the law, and in the light knew him whom she did not see in the darkness. The two women, one of whom burned with love, in the other pretense crept in, figure the Church and the Synagogue or heretical perversity, each of which kills even her own by nourishing them wickedly, and persuades others by enticing them until she destroys them. Between the two women the Lord, while he settles with the spirit of his mouth what is just, restores to each what is due.
3.24: 3.24 He said therefore. RABANUS. Pretending ignorance, he measures human feelings by the dispensation of the flesh, as also there: Where have you laid him? John 20. And elsewhere: Who touched me? Luke 8.
3.25: 3.25 Divide. THE SAME. The Lord tests nature by nature, and wishes according to the will of each to divide the living son between law and grace: not that he approves, but he says he wishes it to rebuke the calumny of the Synagogue.
3.26: 3.26 But she said. THE SAME. The Church, which knows he is hers, willingly yields to her rival that he may live at least with her, lest, divided between law and grace, he be struck by the sword of Christ, hence: Behold, I Paul say to you, that if you keep the law, Christ will profit you nothing, Galatians 5.
4.22: 4.22 The food of Solomon. RABANUS. The refreshment of Christ, who is fed by right faith and good works, which are daily offered to him by the Catholic Church.
4.23: 4.23 Twenty oxen. THE SAME. The preachers of the New Testament, who have in themselves as it were a doubled Decalogue, when they preach the New and Old Testaments equally, full of love of God and neighbor. Besides venison. By the hunting of diverse animals are meant those who from diverse nations are daily caught by the nets of the Gospel through spiritual hunters, and are brought to the feeding of the Savior.
4.26: 4.26 Forty, etc. By forty are designated the times of the ancient law, which Moses, about to receive it, fasted forty days, and the people who were instructed by it were forty years in the desert. And twelve. This number signifies the present time, in which the apostolic teaching nourishes the people of the New Testament.
4.28: 4.28 Barley, etc. Lest anything be lacking in the house of the king, the order of preachers labors in writing and speaking, that it may abound at the table of the Lord, from which the faithful are nourished.
4.32: 4.32 And his songs were. It is agreed that neither the songs nor the disputations of Solomon exist today. Five thousand. On account of the five senses, which he who rules well in various virtues is blessed, and through them as it were sings five thousand songs to the Lord.
4.33: 4.33 Hyssop. RABANUS. Hyssop, a lowly herb clinging to the rock, etc., down to then indeed he bowed the cedar, that is the arrogance of the world, to the humility of hyssop, that is to the foolishness of the cross. And he discoursed. THE SAME. For all things are naked and open to Christ, Hebrews 4. And he disputes when he sets before us the reason of each in his Scriptures, and makes manifest the sacraments which were hidden from ages and generations, that we may consider the blessedness of angels, the usefulness of men, the cunning of demons, and rejecting what is evil, pursue what is good.
5.3: 5.3 And that he could not build a house, etc. BEDE, Questions on the Books of Kings. The house that Solomon built was a figure of the Church, etc., down to in some it shows the struggles of men rewarded with the angels. THE SAME, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 1. This spiritual house is also signified by the tabernacle made in the desert, etc., down to and in many ways shows and figures the salvation of all the nations in Christ.
5.6: 5.6 Command therefore that they cut for me, etc. RABANUS. The servants of Hiram cutting cedars for Solomon from Lebanon, etc., down to they knew the errors of the Gentiles better, and therefore overcame them more skillfully. For you know that there is no man among my people who knows how to cut wood, etc. BEDE, as above. First we must speak of the workmen of the temple, who or whence they were, and of the material itself, etc., down to wheat, namely of the word of God, the oil of charity, of anointing and of the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit.
5.10: 5.10 So Hiram gave Solomon cedar wood and fir wood, according to all, etc. Tyre, whence King Hiram, is an island given to trade, where were the best workers in wood, who gave precious timber receiving food. For they live not by tilling the field but by trading. There is Mount Lebanon, from whose trees the house of the Lord was made. Hence Lebanon also is said there: Open, Lebanon, your gates, Zechariah 11.
5.13: 5.13 And King Solomon chose. BEDE, as above, chapter 3. Not in vain did he choose workmen from all Israel, etc., down to in which the minds of the faithful are regarded by the Lord by daily illumination as the moon by the sun. Workmen from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men. These workmen were proselytes. Their masters were from the Jews, because he did not make anyone of Israel serve.
5.14: 5.14 Adoniram was over this levy. BEDE, ibid. My lord is exalted. This is Christ, who is set over the workmen of the temple, etc., down to that by prayers and fasts it may be worthy of the heavenly inspector and visitor.
5.15: 5.15 And Solomon had seventy thousand who carried burdens, and eighty thousand stonecutters on the mountain. BEDE, ibid. Nor is it to be passed over that the seventy and eighty thousand of burden-bearers and stonecutters with their overseers were not Israelites, etc., down to Some endowed with both virtues come together to the work of the house of the Lord; hence: Rebuke the unquiet, comfort the fainthearted, etc., I Thessalonians 5. Stonecutters. BEDE, ibid. Stonecutters are cutters of stones, etc., down to because rescued from the power of darkness we have come to the citadel of virtues which is in the unity of the Church.
5.16: 5.16 Besides the overseers. The overseers are the makers of sacred Scripture by whose teaching we are trained to teach the ignorant, rebuke the scornful, and bear one another's burdens. Of three thousand. On account of the faith of the Trinity, which the holy words preach. That in Chronicles three thousand six hundred are written, looks to their perfection. For six, in which the adornment of the world was completed, signifies the perfect works of good: and because holy Scripture teaches works of righteousness to be had with faith in truth, rightly the overseers of the works of the temple were three thousand six hundred.
5.17: 5.17 And the king commanded that they take. BEDE, ibid. To build the house of the Lord, first wood and stones are cut from the mountain, etc., down to hence: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Ephesians 2. Great stones. BEDE, ibid., chapter 4. Or the precious stones, great, squared, are the first teachers, who heard the word of salvation from the Lord himself. The layers of stones or wood placed above are the following priests or teachers, by whose preaching the Church grows and is adorned with virtues. RABANUS from Bede. Of what color were the stones, etc., down to the white marble from which the house of the elect is built signifies clean action and conscience chastened from every blemish of corruption; hence: Let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement, etc., II Corinthians 7. For the foundation of the temple. BEDE, ibid. The foundation is Christ, etc., down to that, having cast away superfluous words, deeds, and thoughts, they may become worthy to bear the burden of the Church.
5.18: 5.18 And the Giblites prepared the timber and the stones. RABANUS from Bede, ibid. Gebal is a city of Phoenicia, etc., down to he builds not a sanctuary for the Lord but ruin for himself, who presumes to teach what he has not himself learned. To build the house. THE SAME, ibid. After the foundation composed of such, the house is to be built with the prepared timber and stones, set in order, which have been drawn from their place, because after the first rudiments of faith, after the foundations of humility laid in us by the example of lofty men, the wall of good works must be added upward, and, with courses of stones set upon one another, we must advance from virtue to virtue.
6.1: 6.1 It came to pass therefore. RABANUS from Bede, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 5. A commemoration is made of the going out from Egypt, etc., down to nor Scripture which would intimate the grace of the New Testament in the Old. In the fourth year. In the fourth year of King Solomon the house began to be built: because after the dispensation of the incarnation of Christ, written in the four Gospels, was fulfilled, with the Holy Spirit sent, the structure of the Church began. In the month Zif, which is the same month. BEDE, ibid. That in the second month, etc., down to whence it is clear that as soon as Passover was done he began to build the house of the Lord, and the people, consecrated by the mystical solemnity, put hands to the mystical work. He began to build. THE SAME, ibid. Where the temple was built is made clear in Chronicles, etc., down to but of the interior peace which she had with her Maker she was made possessor. What David had prepared, etc. For David had prepared by singing psalms, other prophets prepared by prophesying a place for the Lord: namely for the true Solomon, in which he would build a house, because they established the hearts of hearers in faith, urging that they should receive with faithful devotion the incarnate Son of God. Hence: Lift up your eyes and see the regions, for they are already white for the harvest: and he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, that he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together, John 4. That he says: Lift up your eyes and see the place that is prepared for building the house, and he who builds by teaching receives wages and gathers precious stones for eternal life: that he who prepares the place for the building and he who builds, that is the prophet foretelling the one to come and the apostle preaching the Lord who has come, may together obtain one reward. In length, etc. The length of the house signifies the longsuffering of the Church, by which she patiently bears adversity until she reaches the homeland. This is of sixty cubits, because six signifies the perfection of good works; because we ought by longsuffering so to bear adversity that through good works we may merit to enter the promised homeland. Twenty cubits. On account of the twofold distance of charity, by which we love God and neighbor. In breadth. Breadth signifies charity, which with enlarged bosom of the mind loves friends in God and enemies for God's sake until, with them converted to peace or wholly destroyed, it rejoices in the Lord with friends alone. BEDE, ibid. Note that the thirty cubits of height did not reach up to the roof of the temple, but to the lower upper room. For it is plainly written in Chronicles that the height was one hundred twenty cubits, about the mysteries of which it will be more fittingly treated in what follows, when the order of reading reaches the middle and third upper room. Thirty cubits. On account of the faith of the Trinity, in the vision of which all the desires of our hope are suspended. Single numbers are multiplied by ten, because through faith and keeping of the law patience is wholesomely exercised: charity burns manfully, and hope is raised sublimely to eternal things. In height. Height signifies the hope of future reward, for which one scorns prosperity or adversity until he sees the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
